STEP 1 - Scene: This is a plate of three strips of cooked, crispy bacon. There is nothing else on it.

STEP 2 - Vessel: The plate is a square white one, about 22 cm on each side. Because it is square, I used side² instead of the circle formula: about 22 × 22 ≈ 480 cm². Allowing for the rounded corners and rim, I took the usable area as about 450 cm².

STEP 3 - Items: The only visible food is three bacon strips. No oil, sauce or dressing is visible.

STEP 4 - Area: The three strips together cover about 15% of the plate, roughly 68 cm².

STEP 5 - Volume: The strips are thin and wavy, so I took an average envelope height of about 0.4 cm. That gives 68 × 0.4 ≈ 27 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Using a bulk density of 0.9 g/ml for meat gives about 24 g. Cooked strips usually weigh about 8 g each, so ~24 g for three strips fits.

STEP 7 - Energy: Cooked bacon is about 540 kcal per 100 g, so 24 g × 5.4 ≈ 130 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: Three crispy strips at roughly 24 g and 130 kcal is plausible for what is visible.
